questions.question: In the Hungarian algorithm, what is a minimum zero cover of a reduced cost matrix?
options: A smallest set of rows and columns that together contain every zero entry
A smallest set of zero entries with no two in the same row or column
A smallest set of rows alone, chosen so that each zero lies in one of them
A set with exactly one covering line through each zero entry of the matrix

questions.question: For the zeros of an $n\times n$ reduced cost matrix, the largest set of zeros with no two in a row or column has 3 elements. How many lines does a minimum zero cover use?
options: One line for each zero entry of the matrix
Exactly $n$ lines, one for every row
As many lines as there are rows with a zero
Exactly 3 lines, the size of that set

questions.question: The marking procedure starts from a maximum set of independent zeros (no two in a row or column, called assigned), marks every unassigned row, then repeatedly marks columns with a zero in a marked row and rows whose assigned zero lies in a marked column. When marking stops, which lines form the minimum cover?
options: Exactly the rows and columns that received a mark
Every marked column and every row left unmarked
The marked rows and the columns that stayed unmarked
All rows, plus every column that stayed unmarked

questions.question: The marking procedure starts from a maximum set of independent zeros (no two in a row or column, called assigned), marks every unassigned row, then repeatedly marks columns with a zero in a marked row and rows whose assigned zero lies in a marked column. Why must the starting set of independent zeros be maximum, not merely one to which no further zero can be added?
options: The marking rules give no lines unless every row is assigned
A larger starting set makes the marking procedure finish faster
From a smaller set the lines can outnumber the assigned zeros
Any starting set works; the choice only changes which lines appear

questions.question: In the Hungarian algorithm for a $5\times5$ cost matrix, a minimum cover of the current zeros uses 4 lines. What follows?
options: A complete zero assignment can be read off at once
A fifth line is added to reach five lines
The row and column reductions are restarted
The uncovered entries must be adjusted first

questions.question: A $4\times4$ reduced cost matrix has zeros exactly at $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, $(3,3)$, $(3,4)$ and $(4,1)$, and the maximum independent zero assignment $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, $(3,3)$ is used. Which rows does the minimum-cover marking procedure mark first?
options: Rows 1, 2 and 3, the rows with assigned zeros
Row 4, the only row without an assigned zero
Row 1, since it contains the most zeros
Rows 2 and 4, whose zeros lie in column 1

questions.question: For the reduced cost matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}4&0&2\\0&0&0\\3&0&5\end{pmatrix}$, the zeros $(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$ form a maximum independent set. The marking procedure marks row 3, then column 2, then row 1. Which lines form the minimum cover?
options: Row 2 and column 2
Rows 1 and 3 and column 2
Column 2 only
Rows 1 and 2

questions.question: After the minimum-cover marking procedure on a $5\times5$ reduced matrix, rows 1, 3 and 5 and columns 2 and 4 are marked. How many lines does the minimum cover use?
options: 5 lines
3 lines
4 lines
2 lines

questions.question: A $4\times4$ reduced cost matrix has zeros exactly at $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, $(3,3)$, $(3,4)$ and $(4,1)$. Which set of lines is a minimum zero cover?
options: Column 1, row 1 and row 3
Rows 2 and 4 with column 1
Columns 1 and 3 with row 1
All four rows of the matrix

questions.question: The Hungarian adjustment is to be applied to $A=\begin{pmatrix}4&0&2\\0&0&0\\3&0&5\end{pmatrix}$, whose zeros are covered by row 2 and column 2. Which value $k$, the smallest entry lying outside both lines, is used?

The marking procedure starts from a maximum set of independent zeros (no two in a row or column, called assigned), marks every unassigned row, then repeatedly marks columns with a zero in a marked row and rows whose assigned zero lies in a marked column. The cover consists of the marked columns and the unmarked rows. Why does it contain every zero?
options: Every zero lies in a marked row, and marked rows are part of the cover
A marked row's zeros lie in marked columns; the rest lie in unmarked rows
Every row becomes marked, so every zero is in some marked column
Zeros occur only at the assigned positions, which the lines contain

questions.question: In an $n\times n$ reduced matrix, a set of $m$ zeros has no two in the same row or column. Why does every cover of all zeros by rows and columns use at least $m$ lines?
options: Each of these $m$ zeros needs both its row and column
Each line contains at most one zero of the matrix
Each line contains at most one of these $m$ zeros
Every cover must use all $n$ rows of the matrix

questions.question: To cover all zeros of a reduced matrix with as few row and column lines as possible, a student repeatedly draws the line containing the most uncovered zeros. Why is the marking procedure used instead?
options: The greedy choice always gives a minimum cover, but more slowly
The greedy choice can need more lines than the minimum cover
The greedy choice can leave some zero entries uncovered
The greedy choice works only when the matrix is not square

questions.question: A $4\times4$ reduced cost matrix has zeros exactly at $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, $(3,3)$, $(3,4)$ and $(4,1)$. Starting from the independent zeros $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, $(3,3)$, the marking procedure is run. Which cover results?
options: Rows 2 and 4 together with column 1
Rows 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the matrix
Columns 1 and 2 together with row 3
Column 1 together with rows 1 and 3

questions.question: In the Hungarian algorithm the reduced matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}4&0&2\\0&0&0\\3&0&5\end{pmatrix}$ has minimum cover row 2 and column 2, and smallest uncovered entry $k=2$. What is the matrix after the adjustment step?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}2&0&0\\0&2&0\\1&0&3\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}2&2&0\\2&4&2\\1&2&3\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}2&0&0\\0&-2&0\\1&0&3\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}2&0&0\\0&0&0\\1&0&3\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: A $4\times4$ reduced matrix has zeros at $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(1,3)$, $(2,1)$, $(3,2)$ and $(4,3)$. Row 1 holds the most zeros. A student draws row 1 first and then keeps drawing the line with the most uncovered zeros. How do the student's line count and the minimum compare?
options: The student uses 4 lines, which is the minimum
The student uses 3 lines, which is the minimum
The student uses 4 lines, but 3 lines suffice
The student uses 4 lines, but 2 lines suffice

questions.question: The marking procedure starts from a maximum set of independent zeros (no two in a row or column, called assigned), marks every unassigned row, then repeatedly marks columns with a zero in a marked row and rows whose assigned zero lies in a marked column. Why does the resulting cover use exactly as many lines as there are assigned zeros?
options: Each final line contains two assigned zeros, so the lines are half as many
Each final line may or may not contain an assigned zero; the counts agree by chance
The cover has one line for every row, so it always uses $n$ lines
Each final line contains exactly one assigned zero, and each one is covered once

questions.question: The marking procedure starts from a maximum set of independent zeros (no two in a row or column, called assigned), marks every unassigned row, then repeatedly marks columns with a zero in a marked row and rows whose assigned zero lies in a marked column. Suppose the procedure marks a column that contains no assigned zero. What does this show?
options: The starting set was not maximum: it can be enlarged by re-matching
Nothing special; that column simply becomes one of the lines
The cover needs one extra row line to remain a cover
The marking must stop at once, as the rules no longer apply

questions.question: A $4\times4$ reduced matrix has zeros at $(1,2)$, $(2,2)$, $(3,1)$, $(3,4)$ and $(4,2)$. Row 3 and column 2 cover all zeros, and $(1,2)$ and $(3,1)$ are independent. What can be concluded without the marking procedure?
options: A cover with a single line might still exist for these zeros
The minimum cover has 2 lines and at most 2 zeros are independent
Three independent zeros might still exist elsewhere in the matrix
Nothing yet; only the marking procedure certifies a minimum cover

questions.question: A $4\times4$ reduced cost matrix has zeros exactly at $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, $(3,3)$, $(3,4)$ and $(4,1)$. Starting from $(1,1)$ and $(3,3)$, to which no zero can be added independently, the marking procedure marks rows 2 and 4, then column 1, then row 1, then column 2. What should be concluded?
options: The lines column 1, column 2 and row 3 are not a cover
A two-line cover exists, matching the two assigned zeros
Column 2 has no assigned zero, so the set can be enlarged
Marking should have stopped once column 1 was marked
